correctness.summary: For each fixed closed hemisphere, Wasserstein distance to measures supported there equals the L^p norm of point-to-hemisphere distance, attained by nearest-point transport. Compact minimization over hemisphere directions gives the exact distance to the full nonsolvable locus. Zhang--Jin's Theorem 1.5 identifies that locus with failure of the affine dual Minkowski problem. Closedness, convexity of the solvable complement, concavity and 1-Lipschitz continuity of the margin follow directly and were checked. The one-sided L^p moment body comparison follows from x<=arcsin(x)<=(pi/2)x, and the W_infinity formula reduces to the centered inradius of conv(supp mu) via support functions and separation.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Zhang--Jin v1 supplies the qualitative hemisphere criterion but no Wasserstein distance-to-degeneracy formula, sharp perturbation radius, nearest bad datum, concavity theorem, one-sided L^p moment body comparison, or W_infinity convex-hull inradius formula was located. Searches combining affine dual Minkowski, closed hemisphere, Wasserstein, robustness, moment-body, and convex-hull/inradius terminology found no matching statement, and no overlap was found in the current SCOPE archive. The fixed-closed-set transport identity and basic support-function facts are standard and are not claimed as new. The most relevant background paper not inspected in full is Cai--Leng--Wu--Xi (2025); its available descriptions concern introduction of affine dual measures and the even problem, so it remains a residual risk rather than evidence of coverage.

value.summary: The result turns a newly completed qualitative existence theorem into an exact perturbation theory in data space: the maximal Wasserstein radius preserving existence is explicit and attained by a concrete adversarial projection. The admissible data form an open dense convex region with a concave 1-Lipschitz depth, while one-sided L^p moment bodies give a dimension-free convex-geometric surrogate and W_infinity robustness has an exact support-hull inradius formula. These features make the criterion directly usable for noisy or approximated measures.

limitations: The result concerns existence robustness of the prescribed measure, not stability or uniqueness of realizing convex bodies.
Wasserstein statements are made after normalizing total mass; positive mass scaling is handled by homogeneity.
No dimension-uniform positive lower bound for the robustness margin holds over all solvable data.
The affine-dual conclusion uses n>=3 and 2<=m<=n-1.
The full text of Cai--Leng--Wu--Xi (2025) was not inspected for a possible explicit Wasserstein robustness statement.
The motivating Zhang--Jin preprint is very recent, so later revisions or unindexed parallel observations may overlap.
Independent audit has not been performed.
